notes:
Summary: enterprise health system evaluating Redwood for clinical documentation search (RAG) with embeddings + reranking. Primary drivers: improve accuracy vs BM25, reduce mean time-to-answer for clinicians, strict PHI controls and auditability.

Scale & perf: initial POC 10k de-identified notes, projected full index ~20M documents (notes + discharge summaries + imaging reports). Target SLO: p95 < 150-200ms for interactive search (clinician-facing) and bulk throughput 200 qps for background queries. Cost sensitivity: aiming for <$0.02 per query (avg) with caching + reranking tiered approach.

Architecture preferences: vector store co-located in VPC or on-prem, embedding model hosted privately, small cross-encoder re-ranker as a second-stage (kept in private deployment). Interested in Redwood Private for residency and audit logs; Dedicated considered for predictable throughput. Must support prefix/KV caching so frequent queries for the same patient are cheap.

Security & compliance notes: full SOC2 and ISO27001 proof required; SSO via SAML mandatory; KMS integration for key separation; detailed per-request audit logs tied to user identity and patient MRN (redacted in logs per legal). Data residency: primary region us-east; legal wants explicit processing map.

POC goals / success metrics: 1) 20%+ MRR improvement in top-3 retrieval relevance vs existing BM25 baseline (reranker included); 2) p95 latency <200ms for interactive; 3) cost per query within target; 4) auditable trail for every retrieval event.

Stated quotes from stakeholders: "We need a solution that scales to millions of notes but never compromises access controls or audit trails." — Dir. Clinical Informatics.

Open technical questions: exact EHR connector approach (HL7/FHIR vs SFTP batch), encryption-at-rest key custody, network egress constraints for embeddings if model hosted off-prem.

Immediate next steps: SE to provision POC cluster (private) + run synthetic 1M doc ingest to validate indexing time and memory footprint; legal to advance DPA review; schedule reranker A/B vs BM25 on week 2 of POC.
